prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near rim of the excavation (about 0.5–2 m away) from its darker interior and the people on the far side (roughly 4–7 m away); in the first frame, the two partly cropped people at left and the person leaning over the near-right rim are among the closest figures, while two standing figures across the pit are farther away and face generally toward the camera side. Across frames 2–3, the nearby people leave the field of view as the camera turns right, while the far-side people, ladder, pit wall, and floor shift left; by frames 4–5, the near ground and rim dominate the right foreground, with the pit and upright reinforcing bars below and farther ahead. Brightness makes distance ordering and the steep drop easier to see than in RGB, including which surfaces are within the camera wearer's arm's reach, but saturated white foreground regions do not preserve useful metric separation. Estimated distances are uncertain because this is monocular depth, and several people, the ladder, thin bars, shadows, and similarly colored wall surfaces have blurred or inconsistent depths.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates multiple person instances in the first three frames, making overlaps clear: two partly cropped people occupy the near-left foreground, another near person leans across the rim to their right, and smaller people stand several metres away across the excavation. It shows which visible fragments belong to separate people even where bodies overlap or extend outside the image, but it supplies no direct range information; RGB and apparent scale suggest the foreground people are about 0.5–2 m from the camera wearer and one another, while the far-side people are roughly 4–7 m away and separated by about 1–3 m. As the view turns right, person masks shift left and disappear, leaving the excavation largely unlabeled; no reliable masks identify the ladder, cables, pit, reinforcing bars, or walls, so reach, height, and front/behind relations for those objects must come from RGB or depth. The large turquoise region labeled "bed" in frame 4 appears to cover sloped ground near the pit rather than a bed and is unreliable, while small truncated person masks at frame boundaries reflect partial views or missed detections rather than complete bodies.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides a usable skeleton only for the close person at the far left of frame 1, placing the torso roughly upright with the upper body leaning toward the pit, one arm extending rightward, and the legs below; the body is approximately 0.5–1.5 m from the camera wearer and the extended hand appears near arm's reach of the adjacent rim or nearby person. Its joint geometry makes limb direction, hand height, and the person's sideways orientation easier to distinguish than in RGB, although it does not establish reliably whether the face or gaze is directed at the camera wearer. Some hand points and lower-limb endpoints are detached or ambiguous, and the head keypoints are incomplete, indicating unreliable localization and occlusion near the image edge. Because frames 2–5 are blank despite visible people in RGB, this map cannot reliably describe their spacing, facing direction, approach or retreat, nor any later change as the camera turns and the people move out of view.
